stages.title: SUBORDINATE ENRICHMENT — ONLY AFTER THE COMPLETE CORE

pills.text: THE ACT GREW OUT OF THE SIMON REPORT
ITS FEDERAL SCHEME FAILED BECAUSE PRINCELY STATES DID NOT
PROVINCIAL AUTONOMY GAVE ELECTED MINISTRIES MORE ROOM THAN UNDER
BUT GOVERNORS RETAINED SPECIAL POWERS, SAFEGUARDS AND DISCRETIONARY AUTHORITY.
THE ACT EXTENDED SEPARATE ELECTORATES AND SPECIAL REPRESENTATION, REINFORCING
COLONIAL PRACTICE OF SEGMENTING THE ELECTORATE BY COMMUNITY AND
NATIONALISTS SAW THE ACT AS A "CHARTER OF SLAVERY"

groups.heading: OPTIONAL SOURCE DEPTH
items: The Act grew out of the Simon Report , RTCs , White Paper (1933) and Joint Select Committee .
Its federal scheme failed because princely states did not accede.
Provincial autonomy gave elected ministries more room than under dyarchy,
but governors retained special powers, safeguards and discretionary authority.

groups.heading: ADVANCED DEBATE
items: The Act extended separate electorates and special representation, reinforcing the
colonial practice of segmenting the electorate by community and interest.
Nationalists saw the Act as a "charter of slavery" even while recognising that elections could be used to mobilise and demonstrate popular support.
CAUTION: Nehru's phrase "a machine with strong brakes but no engine" captured

groups.heading: LEGACY / NUANCE
items: the nationalist critique: constitutional machinery existed, but real sovereignty did not.
Congress debated whether entering ministries would blunt mass struggle or open a new arena for anti-colonial work.
After winning majorities, Congress formed ministries in Bombay, Madras, United Provinces,
Bihar, Central Provinces, Orissa , and later NWFP and Assam .
